reasoning: Recent general-election polling averages show Democrat Ed Markey with a very large lead over likely Republican nominee John Deaton, indicating a strongly Democratic environment for the 2026 Massachusetts Senate race.[3] Primary polling over the last two weeks also consistently finds Markey far ahead of Democratic challenger Seth Moulton, reinforcing that the Senate contest is currently D+ by a substantial margin, while no credible, state-specific general-election presidential polling in the last 45 days emerged from the search, so only the Senate race can be meaningfully assessed.[1][3][6][9][13][8] Given Massachusetts’ structural D+29 Cook Partisan Voting Index and the available Senate polling, the current Senate landscape can reasonably be characterized as roughly D+20–25, with Democrats clearly favored statewide.[3]

sources.name: Pollsmax
sources.details: Pollsmax aggregation of 7 polls reports that Ed Markey leads Republican John Deaton by 23.1 points in its Massachusetts Senate general-election polling average (54.1% D vs 31.0% R), with the latest UNH poll showing Markey ahead 50%-34% (D+16).

sources.name: UMass Amherst/WCVB via WGBH
sources.details: UMass Amherst/WCVB statewide poll of 445 Democratic primary voters finds Ed Markey leading Seth Moulton 60% to 32% in the Massachusetts Democratic Senate primary, a 28-point advantage, described as a double-digit lead and a commanding position.

sources.name: WBUR (reporting UMass Amherst/WCVB poll)
sources.details: UMass Amherst/WCVB poll coverage notes Markey at 60% and Moulton at 32% among likely Democratic primary voters, characterizing Markey’s position as a big lead in the Senate primary.

sources.name: Boston Herald (UMass Amherst/WCVB poll)
sources.details: Boston Herald summary of the UMass Amherst/WCVB poll reports Markey leading Moulton 60% to 32% among self-identified Democratic primary voters, nearly a 30-point gap ahead of the Sept. 1 primary.

sources.name: Suffolk University/Boston Globe
sources.details: Suffolk University/Boston Globe poll of Democratic primary voters finds Markey leading Moulton 52.2% to 38%, a 14.2-point margin, and describes Markey as retaining a wide lead just weeks before the primary.

sources.name: Axios (UMass Amherst/WCVB poll)
sources.details: Axios write-up of the UMass Amherst/WCVB YouGov survey reports Markey ahead of Moulton 60% to 32% among likely Democratic primary voters, calling his lead commanding and noting advantages across key demographic groups.

sources.name: Boston Globe (earlier Suffolk polling context)
sources.details: Boston Globe article on the Senate primary notes prior Suffolk University/Boston Globe polling showing Markey leading among younger voters, reinforcing his standing but referring to an earlier wave outside the most recent 45-day window.

sources.name: RealClearPolling
sources.details: RealClearPolling page for the Massachusetts Democratic Senate primary lists polls and spreads, indicating Markey as the leading candidate in the primary field; it summarizes multiple pollsters consistently showing Markey ahead.

sources.name: Boston.com (UMass Amherst/WCVB poll)
sources.details: Boston.com reports on the UMass Amherst/WCVB poll, stating that Markey has the support of 60% of Democratic primary voters versus 32% for Moulton, with detailed breakdowns by gender, age, and education, and describes Markey as in a strong position heading into the primary.

sources.name: Newsweek (UMass Amherst and Suffolk polling)
sources.details: Newsweek article synthesizes the UMass Amherst poll (Markey 60%, Moulton 32%, D+28) and a Suffolk University/Boston Globe poll (Markey 52%, Moulton 38%, D+14) and notes that both show Markey with a wide lead in the Democratic Senate primary.

sources.name: Ballotpedia
sources.details: Ballotpedia page on the 2026 U.S. Senate election in Massachusetts provides election logistics and candidate listings but does not offer polling or evaluative ratings of candidate strength.

sources.name: PredictionHunt (UNH Survey Center primary poll)
sources.details: PredictionHunt article references a UNH Survey Center poll showing Markey at 41% and Moulton at 35% with 24% undecided earlier in the cycle, indicating a smaller but still positive lead for Markey in the Democratic primary at that time.

sources.name: CNN
sources.details: CNN article on the Massachusetts Democratic Senate primary discusses the generational battle between Moulton and Markey and frames Markey as the incumbent facing a challenge, but it does not provide fresh numeric polling beyond what other outlets report.

sources.name: Boston Globe (UMass Amherst/WCVB poll detail)
sources.details: Boston Globe newsletter notes a UMass Amherst/WCVB poll where 54% said they would vote for Markey and 28% for Moulton (Markey +26) before leaners, and 60% vs 32% (Markey +28) including leaners, underscoring Markey’s wide advantage in the primary.

sources.name: Yahoo News
sources.details: Yahoo News live results page for a Middlesex state Senate seat provides procedural coverage of down-ballot races and does not address the statewide U.S. Senate or presidential contests.
